title: Agent Archivist key-rotation record (archivist.control/v1)
description: The tenant-authority-signed record that documents one client key rotation (plan Section 5: key rotation accepts old and new keys for 24 hours; Phase 3: key rotation with overlapping verification and monotonic authorization epochs). Stored at `tenants/<tenant>/v1/control/rotations/<client>/<epoch>.json`, where the epoch segment is the epoch the rotation establishes, written only by the offline ControlAdminStore, read by ingestion replicas as the durable evidence a rotation leaves behind and as the material a replica needs to verify an old-key attempt inside the overlap without any server-local state. Enforcement rides the linked-client pointer, exactly as revocation does: the rotation is published together with the strictly higher-epoch linked-client record naming the new key, and that pointer bump is what fails stale-epoch attempts closed; this record preserves what the pointer cannot, because a current-pointer object retains no history once it moves — the previous epoch, the previous public key, and both key IDs under the pinned SHA-256 derivation. For the named overlap window of 24 hours from `signed_at`, an attempt presenting the current epoch may sign with either the previous or the new public key, so a retry of an already-frozen envelope re-authorizes with fresh per-attempt state under either half instead of stranding in the spool (plan Section 5; Phase 3 exit gate; EC-12). The flat object is the complete record: the seven wrapper members every immutable control record carries (schemas/v1/control-envelope.json) plus `authorization_epoch` as an identity member — the envelope's write-class rule: an immutable type carries the epoch exactly when it is part of the record's identity, and here it names the established epoch in the object key — plus the rotation payload members, closed with `additionalProperties: false` (docs/notes/control-trust-schemas.md). Public material only, and doubly so: the record carries both public halves and their derivable identifiers, the new private half is generated on the client host and never appears in any record, file, or argument, and the old private half retires with the rotation wherever it lived (SEC-006, ID-001).

x-archivist.signature: control-record-v1 (schemas/v1/control-envelope.json): Ed25519 by the tenant authority named by `authority_key_id` over the RFC 8785 canonicalization of this object with the `authority_signature` member removed. The same construction, key namespace, and verifier core as the linked-client, revocation, and delegation records; domain separation comes from `record_type`, so a rotation can never be replayed as another control record or the reverse.
x-archivist.epochRule: This record's signed `authorization_epoch` is the epoch the rotation establishes — equal to the object key's epoch segment (VAL-002), so a reader holding the linked-client pointer at epoch E finds the overlap evidence for E's key at exactly `rotations/<client>/E.json`. `previous_epoch` equals `authorization_epoch` − 1 (VAL-002 cross-field check): every pointer move publishes the next epoch — the link is epoch 1 and each rotation, scope change, or revocation publishes exactly the next one — so a rotation never skips an epoch. The write is accepted only when the established epoch does not exceed the linked-client pointer's current signed epoch and the pointer at that epoch carries this record's `public_key`: one cannot pre-date a rotation for an epoch the client has not reached, because a forward-dated rotation would arm its overlap window early. The record and the pointer bump that activates it are one administrative act; immutability then makes the history append-only — one object per (client, established epoch), a lost-response retry of identical bytes is an idempotent repair, and no operation removes or rewrites a rotation.
x-archivist.privateKey: both halves here are public — `previous_public_key` survives in this record precisely because verification needs it, and `public_key` is the half the established epoch's linked-client record carries. No private material exists anywhere in this or any other record: the new private half is generated on the client host (ID-001), used there to sign attempts, and reaches nothing else; the old private half dies with the rotation (SEC-006). The gate's banned-name grammar plus the closed shape leave no member for material to ride in.
x-archivist.compatibility: member additions, redefinitions, and new required members are all v2 namespace events — the closed shape is the compatibility rule for control records (docs/notes/control-trust-schemas.md). The only in-place appends this schema tolerates are new tokens inside already-closed enums (record_type in the envelope; key_algorithm through the shared common definition), each shipped together with the readers that understand it

schema.description: The control trust namespace this record belongs to. Pinned by the shared definition; an unknown namespace fails closed before anything else is read.

record_type.description: This is a key-rotation record. Narrowed from the envelope's closed record-type enum to a const of this schema's own token, so this file both names and is the type's complete contract.

record_kind.description: The key-rotation record is an immutable record: written once at the epoch-addressed key derived from its own identifiers, never overwritten — the store rejects an incompatible overwrite outright, so the only writer-visible repetition is a lost-response retry of identical bytes (the envelope's writeClasses rule). Immutability plus epoch addressing is what makes the rotation history append-only: each rotation is its own object at its own established epoch, and there is no way to remove or rewrite one.

tenant_id.description: The tenant whose authority approved this rotation (plan Section 5). Must equal the tenant segment of the object key — the store derives the key from validated fields and refuses any mismatch (ID-008), and a reader can re-make the check, so a record served under another tenant's prefix is rejected as a cross-tenant forgery, not a naming oddity.

client_id.description: The linked client whose authorization key is rotating (ID-001). Must equal the client segment of the object key (VAL-002 cross-field check). The identifier is the one its linked-client record binds — a rotation names the linked installation, never a hostname or any mutable provenance (ID-002).

previous_epoch.description: The epoch this rotation leaves — the last epoch at which the previous key was current. Equals `authorization_epoch` − 1 (VAL-002 cross-field check): every pointer move publishes the next epoch, so a rotation establishes exactly the adjacent epoch and never skips one that would otherwise be unaccounted for. Signed, so a rotation cannot be re-dated onto a different boundary after the fact.

previous_public_key.description: The Ed25519 public half that held at `previous_epoch` — the old half of the overlap. This record is where it survives: the current-pointer linked-client record retains no history once it moves, and a stateless replica verifying an old-key attempt inside the overlap window reads the key here, never from server-local state (plan Section 5; the stateless data plane of Section 3). Public material only (SEC-006).

previous_key_id.description: Identifier of the previous authorization key: the lowercase-hex SHA-256 of `previous_public_key` under the pinned derivation (VAL-002 cross-field derivation, re-made by every verifier — computable from this record's own `previous_public_key`, so the record proves its old key's identity the way the linked-client record proves its current one). Cross-checks against the `uploader_key_id` of attempts signing with the old half inside the window and the `authorization_key_id` of receipts for attempts at `previous_epoch`. A public identifier only — a hash of a public key, never key material (SEC-006).

key_algorithm.description: Algorithm of both public halves; Ed25519 only in v1. One member covers both keys deliberately — v1 has a single token, and the closed enum travels verified inside the authority-signed record, so neither half's algorithm is ever trusted from the attempt. An unknown value fails closed before either key is used.

public_key.description: The new Ed25519 public half — the key of the epoch this rotation establishes, and the value the established epoch's linked-client record carries (VAL-002 cross-record check at the store: this record and the pointer bump that activates it are one administrative act, so the two must agree). The new half verifies from the moment the pointer moves and never stops; the previous half verifies only inside the overlap window below. Public material only (SEC-006): the private half is generated on the client host and never appears in any record, file, or argument.

key_id.description: Identifier of the new authorization key: the lowercase-hex SHA-256 of `public_key` under the pinned derivation, computable from this record's own `public_key` (VAL-002). This is the `uploader_key_id` attempts at the established epoch sign with and the `authorization_key_id` receipts report — one key identity from rotation to receipt — and it equals the `key_id` of the linked-client record at this epoch.

authorization_epoch.description: The established epoch. Identity member of an immutable record (the envelope's write-class rule): it equals the object key's epoch segment in canonical decimal without leading zeros, and the envelope holds this member's bound and that grammar in lockstep — 18 digits at the ceiling (VAL-002 cross-field checks at the store and at any reader). Signed, so a rotation cannot be moved to a different boundary after the fact. An attempt presenting any earlier epoch is stale against the pointer bump that accompanied this record, whatever key it signs with (plan Phase 3 exit gate).

signed_at.description: UTC time the tenant authority signed this rotation, and the anchor of the overlap window: both public keys verify from this timestamp for `rotationVerificationOverlapHours` (24, plan Section 5) — the envelope's named constant, pinned here and proven equal by the gate — after which only `public_key` does. The window widens which key may sign, never which epoch is current: attempts present the current epoch throughout (plan Section 5). Also audit evidence for when the rotation was approved; the epoch sequence is the logical order of the client's authorization history, this is its wall-clock context.

authority_key_id.description: Identifier of the tenant authority key that signed this record — the root the rotating client pinned during linking (ID-009). Names which pinned key (or, once authority rotation exists, which authority record's key) verifies `authority_signature`; see the envelope's authority-chain rule. A rotation signed by any other key is not a rotation.

authority_signature.description: The tenant authority's Ed25519 signature under the control-record-v1 construction (schemas/v1/control-envelope.json): the RFC 8785 canonicalization of this object with this member removed. The one field the authority itself cannot cover, and the reason the client, both epochs, both key identities, and the overlap's anchor are tamper-evident — an attacker holding only the raw-data or control-reader credential cannot forge, alter, or extend a rotation window.
